title: the Nine Hells
audit_comment: THE NINE HELLS, printed pp. 109-113, the plane of evil organized to further its own malefic ends: nine infinite layers, the barriers at the lowest point of the upper and half a mile above the next below (the flightless falling the 20d6 cap into spectacular attention), the physical laws constant within each layer but changing between them. The layers: Avernus the front parlor, dark red starless sky, flammable vapor gathered in dimly glowing spheres bursting into fireballs at 1-in-6 per turn (1-in-12 without open flame), Tiamat the watchdog and her astrally-projecting crags; Dis the Iron City of Dispater, its stone-and-lead sanctum beyond the barriers, green-overcast lightning skies; Minauros Mammon's stinking sinking city at 13% disease per visit, its barrier to Dis 30 feet above the palace roofs; Phlegethos the liquefied-fire realm of Belial and Abriymoch, the Mount of Leaping Flames; Stygia the frozen sea of the diluted Styx, the three-mile ice pack over the limitless ocean, Geryon's Tantlin lit by dancing lightning and 2d6 walls of cold fire; Malbolge the rockfall of Moloch the viceroy, copper-shod fortresses under blood-red steam; Maladomini of Baalzebul, quarries and lava aqueducts, Malagard the thousand-mile million-room palace over a dungeon vaster than the devils know; Caina at -60 degrees under Mephistopheles; and Nessus, the vast rifts descending to Asmodeus's palace, dwarfing the Khin-Oin, on the banks of the shifting ice lake fed by the Lethe - extremes of cold, heat and cliff, triple-strength waves of fire turning all to ash. The paths: the Styx through Avernus into Stygia, the Lethe of Nessus (black waters as the Styx but Charon never there), the identical reddish-hoop portals of Avernus to Acheron, Gehenna and Concordant Opposition guarded by Tiamat's abishai and traps, the many Prime conduits whose squabbling dooms evil's plans, and the rumored pre-overlord conduit in the palace's heart that destroys all evil that touches it - the reason the stories say the best escape from the Hells is to journey to the lowest layer. The devils: the rigid caste, the MM2 layer frequencies, the home-layer immunity (the Caina ice devil cold-immune only in Caina), the arch-devils as lesser gods of their home planes whose lust to rule in Hell outweighs defeating good. The politics: Asmodeus of layers 1, 5 and 9 with Geryon and Tiamat; Baalzebul of 4, 6 and 7 with Moloch and the recruited Belial; Mephistopheles the reasonable with Dispater and Mammon of 2, 3 and 8 - the overlord weakest-seeming yet supreme, playing faction against faction, holding both ends of the Hells through the underrated Tiamat. And the other Powers: Druaga tolerated on Dis's layer; Set's blazing bone-dry swath of Avernus and his pyramid of captive labor between the Hells and Acheron; Hecate and Inanna adjacent in Phlegethos, the organized punisher and the fickle belligerent, both courts called on by Belial and both dreaded by Asmodeus; Sekolah beneath Stygia's ice devouring Geryon's ambassadors; Kurtulmak robbing his suitors blind; No Cha the nocturnal thief forever moving; and the false-name devils - the devil Dagon and the devil Nergal - muddling who rules the lower planes, as Titivilus tells it: Nergal lives in the Hells, outcast, hides in Avernus, looks like a toad, poor thing.

consts.name: ddpHellsLayerCount
consts.comment: the nine layers of the Hells, each infinite, extending forever in all directions; the barriers between layers always sit at the lowest point of the upper layer and at a very high point above the surface of the next below (the convenient mountain descents very rare and always guarded - otherwise the barrier exit hangs about a half-mile above the next layer, and the flightless fall for the 20d6 cap and the spectacular attention of the creatures below); the physical laws and properties of matter are constant within each layer but change from layer to layer.

consts.name: ddpAvernusFireballChance
consts.comment: the Avernus fireball vapor: the front parlor's dark red starless sky over a rocky wasteland of stunted twisted plants, its atmosphere filled with flammable vapor gathered into innumerable dimly glowing spheres - a 1 in 6 chance per turn that a glowing region bursts into a fireball (as the spell) for 2-7 dice of damage, reduced to 1 in 12 if the traveler refrains from open flame; the great rocky crags shelter greater devils astrally projecting, and Tiamat watches the parlor.

consts.name: ddpMinaurosDiseasePct
consts.comment: the Minauros disease: the third layer of the avaricious under Mammon, marsh and wet ground under continual rains, hail and sleet, the only solid land the hard volcanic ridges undulating like frozen serpents - the black-stone sinking city continually settling into the swamps, a barrier to Dis only 30 feet above Mammon's palace roofs and carefully guarded, the surrounding ground rotten with decaying bodies that halve movement rates - and the most disease-ridden of the lower planes, a 13% chance per visit that an extraplanar traveler contracts a disease.

consts.name: ddpStygiaIceMiles
consts.comment: the Stygia ice: the fifth layer, a great frozen sea through which the Styx cuts a clear channel (losing its memory-robbing power here by dilution), eons of decayed moss and small plants producing a cold swamp atop an ice pack up to three miles in thickness floating on an ocean of limitless depth; the solid ground is the floating islands, from whose peaks lightning dances out of the jet black sky and walls of cold fire radiating 2d6 points of damage guard the barriers to the upper Hells.

consts.name: ddpMalagardMiles
consts.comment: the Malagard of Maladomini: the seventh layer, Baalzebul's home, a solid surface twisted and deformed by continual building and rebuilding - great quarries scarring the countryside, stone-walled aqueducts and canals carrying lava across the lifeless plains, malebranche fortresses and city ruins dotting the land; the only inhabited city is Malagard, a palace stretching a thousand miles and containing a million rooms, over a dungeon complex so vast the devils themselves are unaware of its full dimensions.

consts.name: ddpCainaCold
consts.comment: the Caina cold: the eighth layer outdoes Stygia in heartless cold - a region of huge glaciers moving past mountains of slower-moving ice, snow and sleet continual companions, and travelers suffer the effects of -60 degree weather (per the WSG) as long as they remain; the ruler is Mephistopheles.

bools.name: ddpHellsDoctrine
bools.comment: the Nine Hells doctrine: the plane of evil organized to further its own malefic ends, dominating the imagination of travelers, the greed of treasure-seekers, and the battle-fury of paladins - the devils set in a rigid caste system amid large numbers of other evil creatures; the Hells are the most typical of the lower planes, so much so that the unknowing ascribe their environments to the other lower planes as well.

bools.name: ddpNineLayersRule
bools.comment: the nine layers: Avernus the front parlor (Tiamat's lair of abishai and evil dragon spirits); Dis the Iron City rising miles over low hills and black stagnant rivers, the stone-and-lead inner sanctum of Dispater beyond its barriers, the flat barren land under a dull green overcast lit by lightning; Minauros Mammon's sinking city; Phlegethos the nightmare realm of volcanos and rivers of liquefied fire (entering one means the plane of elemental Fire), ruled by Belial from Abriymoch, the Mount of Leaping Flames, a basalt palace in a dead volcano whose tunnels are far larger than the outside allows; Stygia the frozen sea of Geryon's Tantlin; Malbolge the huge rockfall of city-sized angular black stones over a possible infinite lava sea, the copper-shod fortresses of Moloch the viceroy of Baalzebul beneath blood-red steam clouds; Maladomini of Baalzebul and Malagard; Caina the glacier layer of Mephistopheles; and Nessus, the final level - a series of vast rifts each leading lower to the grand palace of Hell's Overlord Asmodeus, dwarfing even the Khin-Oin, resting on the banks of a great shifting lake of ice fed by the river Lethe, a land of extremes: the coldest regions, the hottest volcanos, the steepest and smoothest cliffs, and waves of fire as triple-strength walls sweeping the region and turning everything in their path to ash - a recommended stop only in the most dire of needs.

bools.name: ddpHellsPortals
bools.comment: the paths in and out of the Hells: the Styx runs through Avernus and into Stygia with Charon and his charonadaemons ferrying the foolish; the Lethe runs through Nessus, said to link to certain Prime Material planes as the Yggdrasil and Olympus link theirs (unknown whether it does) - its black waters work as the Styx but Charon and his servants never appear on its shores; Avernus holds portals to the topmost layers of Acheron and Gehenna and to the outer rings of Concordant Opposition, identical free-standing hoops of reddish light that Tiamat guards with abishai encampments and traps; a large number of conduits lead to Prime Material planes so the dukes and archdukes can vie for control of evil across the alternates - squabbling that spells the doom of evil plans, for evil always turns upon itself; and in the heart of Asmodeus's palace a rumored conduit older than any overlord that destroys all evil that touches it, even the mightiest arch-devil or demon prince - destination unknown, the foundation of the stories that the best escape from the Hells is to journey to the lowest layer.

bools.name: ddpDevilRule
bools.comment: the devil rule: devikind the most prominent inhabitants, sharing the plane with many other evil creatures (the Monster Manual II devil entry the summary of frequencies by layer); all creatures native to the Nine Hells are unaffected by the natural forces of their native layer - the ice devil of Caina immune to all magical and natural cold, but only while in Caina - a home advantage that tends to prevent attacks by devils from other layers; the arch-devils are a group of powerful devils, treated as lesser gods in their home plane, dedicated to the defeat of good and their own supremacy over all the known planes - a unified force that could pose a great problem, except that each is convinced that he (or she) alone is the most capable leader of the diabolic forces: the desire to rule in Hell always outweighs any advantage from defeating the forces of good (devils contest with Odin, but no devil sees himself taking Odin's position in Gladsheim), and all see themselves as contenders for the Overlord's throne - the battling more subtle than the roaring wars of the Oinodaemon's halls, but endless in the pits nonetheless.

bools.name: ddpArchdevilPolitics
bools.comment: the arch-devil census and politics: Asmodeus the overlord ruling from the great palace in Nessus's lowest rift, his household and staff not fully described, to his liking; Mephistopheles in the iron citadel of Mephistar overlooking the great glacier Nargus, Hutinin his chief duke; Baalzebul, the second-most powerful, in Malagard's maze of towers walls and dungeons jammed with treasure and never-thrown-out debris; Moloch, Baalzebul's vassal denied a permanent home, moving location to location across Malbolge; Geryon's castle Tantlin rising from the Stygian ice, Armon his chief assistant; Belial's basalt Abriymoch in a dead volcano's cone; Mammon in the stinking sinking Minauros, served by Bael his chief commander and Glasya his chief consort, one of the more powerful diabolic members of the Hells; Dispater's stone tower in the heart of Dis, gathering information from his erinyes in the highest towers and dictating to Titivilus his trusted messenger; Tiamat's cavernous Avernus lair of abishai and evil dragon spirits sent to lay low the challengers. Politically three opposing groups: Asmodeus commands the unswerving loyalty of Geryon and Tiamat (layers 1, 5 and 9); Baalzebul with Moloch his stated vassal recruiting Belial, whose rivalry with Geryon is unbounded (layers 4, 6 and 7); Mephistopheles the would-be force of reason and restraint with Dispater and the ever-greedy Mammon (layers 2, 3 and 8). Asmodeus seems weakest but holds the overlord's control: his rivals cannot depend on their factions (members defy Asmodeus only when victory is certain, arch-devils quickly turn on erstwhile allies for gain), the faction not revolting automatically sides with him hoping for spoils, and he plays one against the other, never letting his dukes know where they stand - plus his control of both ends of the Hells through Tiamat, underrated by her compatriots as a dumb beast.

bools.name: ddpHellsPowers
bools.comment: the non-devil Powers of the Hells: the organized realms are vast but the layers infinite, home to other Powers - the true relationship between lawful evil Powers and devils unknown, each world ignorant of the other's rivals (Tiamat as Takhisis never lets her Krynn followers know there are other arch-devils or a Nine Hells at all, and Asmodeus keeps the Druagas and Sets of the multiverse unknown to his own); Druaga, the self-titled Ruler of the Devil World, a Babylonian lesser Power with a realm on the second layer far from Dis's hills, tolerating and tolerated by Dispater, who may provide the devils Druaga sends forth; Set of the Egyptians, whose single-minded vengeance against Osiris, Horus and the pantheon exceeds even Loki's hatred of Gladsheim, accepting no equals - too weak to be driven from the Hells but not strong enough to have come, he controls a large swath of Avernus lit by a blazing sun and bone-dry as the desert, his great white-stone palace overseeing captives erecting a massive pyramid he hopes will fill his layer and create his own set of planes between the Hells and Acheron - dangerously close to a mad god; Hecate of the Greeks and Inanna of the Sumerians with adjacent realms in Phlegethos and conduits to their worshiping worlds - Hecate more lawful than evil, sending her devil quota out in organized fashion to punish particular misdeeds, Inanna more evil than lawful, delighting in the fickle blessings of too many or not enough servants in battle, both indifferent to their organized neighbors, both courts called on by Belial, both feared by Asmodeus (who would rather cut off a limb than see the Greek and Sumerian pantheons descend on his delicate balance); Sekolah, the great white shark of the sahuagin, abiding in Stygia's deep oceans far beneath the ice pack, dining on giant sea-beasts and known to surface to converse with - and often devour - Geryon's ambassadors to the monarch of the deep; Kurtulmak of the kobolds in the first layer's caverns, careful to stay out of the way, courted by arch-dukes as one more ally, smiling graciously, taking all aid, and robbing the arch-devils blind while maintaining his front - rarely admitting to his followers that his Hells have any other major inhabitants; No Cha of the Chinese, a demi-god with no set address like Ratri in the glooms of Hades, invoked by thieves and robbers for nocturnal luck, always moving, stealing from one devil group and seeking sanctuary with another, smart enough not to steal anything someone would start a war to recover (Asmodeus's rod of office, for example); and the false-name doctrine - lesser devils given the names of Powers (the devil Dagon who is not the demon prince, the devil Nergal who is not the Babylonian god) to upset the other Power, to catch spell casters invoking without understanding, and to muddle who rules the lower planes - as Titivilus says: Nergal? Why, Nergal lives in the Hells - outcast, hides in Avernus, looks like a toad, poor thing.
